featured_reviews.review_text:
Village Side Cafe is a unique hangout spot in Borivali with a rustic, village-themed vibe that makes it stand out from typical cafés. The ambience is quite lively, especially in the evenings with live music and performances, making it a good place to chill with friends.

The food menu offers a mix of North Indian, Chinese, and continental dishes. While the taste is decent and some items like starters are enjoyable, the quality can be a bit inconsistent at times.

One of the highlights is the overall vibe—open seating, music, and a relaxed atmosphere. It’s especially popular among groups looking for a late-night hangout spot since it stays open till late.

However, the location can be slightly difficult to access, and the road conditions nearby aren’t the best. Some visitors have also mentioned issues with service, billing, and management during busy hours.

Overall, it’s a good place for ambience and music, but there’s room for improvement in service and consistency.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Pirates Cafe, Borivali West with family and unfortunately had one of the most disappointing café experiences in recent times.

We ordered Coconut Cream Matcha, Special Thandai Ice Latte Signature, Cold Coffee Signature Tiramisu, Cold Coffee Café Mocha (Cold), Parmesan & Roasted Garlic Fries, along with other beverages. The drinks were average at best, while the fries were decent but nowhere close to compensating for the poor service experience.

The biggest issue was the attitude of the management. We were initially seated in the open-air section and requested a table in the AC section. However, once our order had been placed, there was absolutely no effort from the owners to accommodate the request. It felt as though, after securing the order, customer comfort became irrelevant.

The tables provided were also problematic. Two tables of different dimensions had been joined together, and both were continuously shaking because of uneven bases. Such basic maintenance issues reflect poorly on the attention given to customer experience.

What made the visit even more frustrating was the serving sequence. We ordered multiple beverages and fries together, expecting a family coffee outing where everyone could enjoy their orders at the same time. Instead, every item arrived separately with gaps of around five minutes. By the time the last beverage arrived, the first few drinks had already been consumed. This completely defeated the purpose of visiting a café as a group.

The staff appeared more focused on pleasing the owners than on delivering good customer service. Genuine hospitality was missing, and customer concerns were clearly not a priority.

To add to the irony, a table in the AC section was finally offered only when the last beverage was being served. It came across as artificial courtesy and fake empathy rather than a sincere attempt to resolve the issue.

Overall, an extremely bad experience. There are plenty of cafés that understand customer comfort, service quality, and hospitality far better than this place.

My rating reflects the attitude of the owners towards customers.

Looking at this review and rating, I expect the owners may respond with sympathy and explanations, but what customers need is better service and genuine concern, not post-review damage control.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Pibati is a charming little find for anyone who enjoys thoughtfully curated vegetarian food and well-made coffee. What instantly stands out is that the entire menu is 100% vegetarian, which is a big plus for people who specifically look for veg-friendly cafés without compromise on flavours or creativity.

We ordered quite a spread, starting with the Masala Avocado Toast, which was fresh, flavourful, and perfectly spiced without overpowering the natural taste of avocado. The Raw Papaya & Mango Bhel was a refreshing surprise — a lovely mix of crunch, tang, and sweetness that worked beautifully as a light starter. The Tadka Hummus had a desi twist and paired nicely with the accompaniments. For mains, the Aglio Olio Pasta was comforting, well cooked, and balanced in flavour. To finish, we enjoyed the Tiramisu Coffee and a Classic Cappuccino — both were satisfying and well brewed. We wanted to try their Matcha offerings, but we didn't order once they told us they still don't use Bree Matcha as their source of Matcha & we didn't want to risk having a bad Matcha experience.

Every dish we ordered tasted good, though the serving sizes could definitely be a little more generous, especially considering the pricing. One unique and interesting find was the Ghee Roast Croissant, which stood out for its creativity and flavour.

Seating-wise, the café has a small indoor area that accommodates around 15 people with roughly 6 compact tables, so it can feel a bit tight during peak hours. The outdoor seating is designated for smokers, so it’s best avoided if you’re visiting with kids. The service was prompt and courteous, which added to the overall positive experience.

Unfortunately, we were extremely hungry and only managed to click photos of the avocado toast before everything else arrived! Overall, Cafe Pibati is a great stop for vegetarian food lovers looking for quality food, good coffee, and a cozy café vibe — just with slightly limited seating and portion sizes. ✅☕🥑

It had only been a little over an hour since I arrived when Yash, one of the stewards, approached me and asked if I would be ordering anything else, otherwise I would need to clear the table because there were people on the waitlist.
This was quite shocking, especially since I still had coffee left on the table and had only just finished my food. When I told him that I was still having my coffee and asked how I could be expected to order more, he simply repeated that there were guests waiting.
What made the situation even more confusing was that there were other tables around me that had nothing on them and those customers were not asked to move. In fact, another table cleared up just a couple of minutes after this conversation, and no new customer occupied that space for the rest of the time I was there.
When I asked another steward what the issue was, he mentioned that on weekends customers are not allowed to use the Wi-Fi for more than 60 minutes. This was never communicated anywhere in the café.
I had been a regular at Pibatie until this incident, but the way this situation was handled made me feel unwelcome.
You’ve definitely lost a loyal customer

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Detailed Review – Gosssip Corner, Borivali West

Visited Gosssip Corner in Borivali West and had a very enjoyable experience. The café is popular for its huge variety of vegetarian dishes, creative presentations, and lively ambience. It is a good place for family outings, friends’ gatherings, birthday celebrations, and casual dining.

🍽️ Food Variety:
The menu is extremely large with options from Italian, Mexican, Continental, Café-style snacks, pizzas, sandwiches, sizzlers, mocktails, desserts, fondue, Jain food, and fusion dishes. One of the biggest attractions is their unique presentation and experimental menu. Popular dishes include Hummus Platter, Cheese Garlic Bread, Nachos, Greek God Pizza, Chilly Garlic Fries, Corn Cheese Momos, Brownie Shake, Fondue options, and creative fusion snacks.

💰 Price Per Person:
Approx ₹400–₹800 per person depending on the order. For a group dining experience with mocktails and desserts, the bill can be slightly higher, but portion sizes are generally good.

🏠 Ambience:
Ambience is one of the strongest points. The café has a cozy, artistic, and vibrant atmosphere with comfortable seating and modern décor. It has a lively vibe, especially during evenings and weekends. Good for photographs and celebrations.

👨‍🍳 Staff & Service:
Staff members are generally friendly, polite, and helpful. Service is usually good, though during peak hours there can be some waiting time because of heavy crowd. Many customers appreciate the support provided by the team for special food preferences including Jain options.

🚗 Parking:
Parking availability depends on the branch. Limited parking is available nearby, and during weekends finding a spot can be slightly difficult. Better to arrive early during peak hours.

🧼 Cleanliness & Hygiene:
Overall cleanliness is maintained well considering the crowd. Seating, serving style, and food presentation are good.

📍 Location:
Conveniently located in Borivali West near Yogi Nagar and easily accessible from Link Road.

📌 Overall:
Excellent café with huge food variety, creative dishes, good ambience, and enjoyable dining experience. Perfect place for food lovers who enjoy trying different fusion and café-style dishes.

Highly recommended 👍

featured_reviews.name: Perpetual Gomes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Slow in Kandivli recently with my cousin sister, and honestly, while the food and coffee were good, the overall experience and service left us extremely uncomfortable.

When we entered, there were multiple empty 4-seater tables available (which remained empty throughout most of our visit), yet we were seated at their “community table”  which is essentially a tiny circular table against the wall that is genuinely not practical for two people ordering food and drinks.

One of the waiters later moved us to a proper table after realizing the issue, but shortly after, someone managing the cafe asked the waiter to move us back to the tiny community table again. We even mentioned that it would be difficult to comfortably eat there once food arrived, but were told “it will be fine.”

Unfortunately, it really wasn’t.

Things kept falling while we were eating because there simply wasn’t enough space. We had to move the cutlery setup ourselves just to make room for the plates and drinks. Nobody checked in or offered any solution despite clearly seeing the inconvenience.

What honestly made the experience worse was noticing another individual sitting alone with camera equipment/content setup being comfortably given a larger table while we, as paying customers ordering food and coffee, were repeatedly denied one despite tables remaining vacant throughout our meal.

If the cafe had been full, this would’ve been understandable. But it wasn’t.

The food itself was genuinely good and reasonably priced, which makes this more disappointing because the experience could have been great with just basic consideration and hospitality.

Also adding a service charge after this experience honestly felt a little absurd.

I hope the cafe improves how they treat regular customers moving forward because good food alone isn’t enough to make people return.

Felt so bad about the extra calories and 400 bucks going down the drain for this whereas a small sachet of Tiggle does a WAYYY better job at home. I even requested the server if I could get a stronger version of chocolate by tweaking it after having just one sip but he refused by saying that the jaggery/palm sugar already comes mixed with the chocolate so there's nothing they can do about it.
The burrito bowl was average, not bad but nothing I'd go again for. And the nachos were a bit stale, so much for "fresh and from scratch" ingredients.
The broccoli and cottage cheese burger didn't feel like it had any cottage cheese but rather just broccoli and mushed potatoes. The hand cut fries that came with it were too salty, oily and soggy.
Lastly, the spiced orange cream iced latte only sounded fancy and had cream chunks instead of a well frothed foam on top.
The only good parts were that the ambience has been tastefully decorated and the service is quick.

featured_reviews.name: Avni Barai
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is by far one of the best places in Borivali to just go and chill for a while sipping on some good teas and other beverages and munching on some good snacks while chit chatting or playing board games or ready books! ☺️😻

Went here after soo long with my mom and dii for some evening tea and snacks.

The place was really crowded. Make sure you pre book or you'll have to wait for atleast half an hour in case you wanna sit inside. They have such beautiful sittings inside and upstairs too. They also have sittinh outside.

They have so many board games like ludo, chess, snakes and ladders and even cards to play and enjoy!

We started by ordering their ginger kadak tea and hazelnut coffee.

The tea was just so soothing and amazing and the prominent flavour of ginger made it even better!
Also, the hazelnut coffee was so yummm! Loved it!!

For food, we started by ordering their desi style nachos and loaded fries. These were the best best dishes😻 Nachos were soo yum and proper desi style! Also the quantity of the fries served were really huge! The fries tasted so delicious and so cheesy! Don't miss out on their loaded fries in case you're visiting this place!

We also ordered Pizza which was cheesy and delicious and the crust and topping were tooo goood!

We also tried their aloo cheese parathas with dal makhni! 😻 Soft and delicious parathas with hot dal makhni.. just perfect!!!

We even went for Cheese chilli toast! In case you're a cheese lover... this is a must try! 😻

To end our perfect evening, we tried their nutella waffles. Freshly baked waffles drizzled with nutella and chocolate sauce and topped with vanilla icecream.. they were so yumm and not too hard and not too soft.. just perfect!

If you're ever looking for a place to hangout in Borivali, this should be it!

Also, they have come with up an exciting challenge recently... if you eat six biscuits in a minute altogether, then the bill is on them! Do try this challenge😻👍🏻

The Hazelnut Blast Coffee is an absolute must-try if you’re a fan of nutty flavors. It’s rich, smooth, and has the perfect balance of hazelnut sweetness that doesn’t overpower the coffee itself. For those who like a touch of indulgence, the Bronze Frost Coffee offers a delightful creamy texture with a hint of chocolate, giving a luscious experience that feels like a dessert in a cup.

To complement the drinks, their pasta is a great choice. The dish is hearty with a comforting, homestyle flavor that pairs well with their coffee options. It’s not overly saucy but just enough to coat each bite, leaving you satisfied without feeling too heavy.

Overall, the new Love n Latte outlet in Borivali is a fantastic spot for coffee lovers, with its thoughtful menu and cozy atmosphere, making it an easy go-to for casual meetups or quiet escapes.

⭐ Rating: 3/5

I had heard amazing reviews and seen so many reels about Kaffeine’s pizza 🍕, but honestly, it didn’t quite live up to the hype. The pizza came with uneven toppings, very little sauce, and was slightly burnt . I had also asked for extra olives, but they were missed .

On the brighter side ✨, the Peri Peri Hummus was really good — perfectly spiced and flavorful 😋. The Tomato Soup 🍅 was also one of the best I’ve had! The Nachos 🌮 were decent (3.5/5) — could use a bit more authentic touch, especially the salsa and sour cream. The Chilly Garlic Noodles 🍜 were okay, but the garlic flavor was a bit too strong and overpowered the noodles.

Service could definitely improve — I was told to order by 11:15 PM, and when I called at 11:10, they had already stopped taking orders 😔.

Overall, it’s a nice place with good vibes, but the food and service didn’t quite match the expectations this time. Hoping for a better experience next visit! 🌿💫
